E29 Sink Project

Project Overview

Worked with a team of engineers to design a sink attachment to aid in hand-washing dishes. This project was done through UC Berkeley's E29 course.

Skills Used

CAD SOLIDWORKS Documentation Technical Presentation 3D Printing Project Management

Project Type - UC Berkeley Collaborators - Trent Frandson, Minou Bouman, Nilesh Kothari, Aarav Bedi, Ottis Pendergraft

The Sink Project was a project designed to help gain experience in GD&T, manufacturing techniques, and engineering drawing. The device itself was an accessory that could be attached to a kitchen sink. When the integrated soap bottle was filled with soap, the water from the sink would mix with it to produce soapy water for cleaning dishes. The device was intended to aid those who didn’t have a dishwasher.

The project was designed in SOLIDWORKS and 3D printing on a Formlabs SLA printer using clear resin. Additional components were purchased off-the-shelf.

Specific tolerance fits were used for this project. First, a locational clearance LC2 fit was designed to ensured that the soap bottle would fit snugly to the mixing chamber while still allowing for diassembly. Second, a sliding fit LC11 fit was designed to allow the cap to fit over the soap reservoir but be easily diassembled.
